solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Early Stones – such as could make a man of Jon?

blocks.note: the opening letter of the name, the one that has to be replaced
'such as' shortens to the comparing word
putting these four letters where the J stands turns the name into PERSON, a man

explanation.surface: A rock-history quiz asks which early Rolling Stones line-up could turn someone called Jon into a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'J as PERS': swap J for PERS and JON becomes PERSON, a man. Run together, J AS PERS spells JASPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque quartz prized as a gemstone since antiquity, so jaspers are stones used from the earliest times.

clue.text: Take drugs ‘recreationally’ and amuse oneself switching parts?

indicators.note: the two halves of the word change places

blocks.note: popjoy is an old verb meaning to amuse oneself

explanation.surface: A user dabbles in drugs for fun and has a good time swapping roles.
explanation.walkthrough: POPJOY swaps its halves to make JOYPOP.
explanation.definitionFit: To joypop is to take a habit-forming drug occasionally, for pleasure, without becoming addicted.

clue.text: Jap Mister going round seraglio? He enjoys some profit from catch

definitions.text: He enjoys some profit from catch

indicators.note: one word goes round the other, enclosing it

blocks.note: san is the Japanese honorific added to a name, like Mister
a seraglio is a harem

explanation.surface: A Japanese gentleman tours a harem, and someone profits from what is caught.
explanation.walkthrough: S(HAREM)AN. 'Catch' looks like a romantic catch in the harem; it is a haul of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A shareman is a member of a fishing crew paid with a share of the takings rather than wages.

clue.text: Piano medley creating something akin to paraplegia?

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
an olio is a mixture or miscellany

explanation.surface: A medley of piano pieces is so bad it leaves the audience paralysed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'medley' looks like an anagram signal but is simply OLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Poliomyelitis can cause paralysis of the limbs, so it is related to paraplegia, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Fiery song represented scarlet description of dawn

indicators.note: to represent is to present again in a new form, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
scarlet is a red colour

explanation.surface: A blazing song paints the dawn in scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rosy-fingered Dawn' is Homer's stock epithet in the Iliad and Odyssey.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer repeatedly calls the dawn rosy-fingered, picturing pink streaks of light spreading across the morning sky.

clue.text: Aromatic umbellifer showing sound quality in boxes on meadow (12, two words)

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: to spar is to box
tone is the quality of a sound
a ley is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: A fragrant plant reveals its tonal quality in boxes laid out on a meadow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' looks like containers, but it is the verb: to spar is to box. A ley is grassland, often spelt lea.
explanation.definitionFit: Stone parsley is a hedgerow plant of the carrot family with aromatic seeds, a member of the umbellifers.

clue.text: He struck a dangerous bargain, making money round the States

indicators.note: one word goes round, enclosing the other, which sits inside it

blocks.note: fat is a slang term for money or profit
the United States, abbreviated

explanation.surface: Someone takes a risky deal, earning money all around America.
explanation.walkthrough: Fat as slang for money or profit is old and mainly found in Chambers, as in 'fat cat'.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend Faust sold his soul to the Devil in exchange for knowledge and power, the most famous perilous pact.

clue.text: Swag one removed from blown safe, extremely new

indicators.note: what is removed from a word is taken out of it
a blown safe has been blasted apart, so its letters are scattered

blocks.note: a means one; this letter is removed
the word the letter comes out of
too means excessively, extremely
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A burglar's loot: one item taken from a safe blown open, brand new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swag' looks like a burglar's loot from the blown safe, but here it is the decorative sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A swag is a hanging chain of flowers or fabric looped between two points, which is exactly what a festoon is.

clue.text: A learner on piano has cut short beginning

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the learner driver's plate
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
taken as written before its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A novice at the piano has had to abandon their first steps early.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha is the first letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is used for the first part or start of something, as in alpha and omega.

clue.text: Lads in NE Scotland upended local doormat?

indicators.note: turned on end in a down entry, the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: loon is the north-east Scots word for a lad

explanation.surface: Young men in Aberdeenshire flip over the doormat of the local pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local' signals a dialect word, not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Snool is a Scots word for a cringing, submissive person, someone others walk over like a doormat.

clue.text: Local maybe in exclusive group up for sport

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
in a down entry, going up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: a set is a clique or exclusive circle
a local is one's neighbourhood pub, and an inn is one example

explanation.surface: The neighbourhood pub, perhaps, is part of a smart crowd who are keen on games.
explanation.walkthrough: S(INN)ET reads upwards as TENNIS. A local is British slang for the pub nearest one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket game played over a net, one of the best-known sports.

clue.text: Unconventional marriage (busy one not available: husband)

blocks.note: a bee is proverbially busy
N/A is the abbreviation for not available
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: An unusual match: the busy partner never around, leaving only the husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Beenah is a form of marriage, found in Sri Lanka, in which the husband lives with the wife's family, the reverse of the usual custom.

clue.text: Muslin etc, No. 1 in outre fashioned thread

indicators.note: the number one letter of a word is its opening letter
something fashioned has been shaped or made anew, so the letters are worked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of outre
a line is a thread or cord

explanation.surface: A list of fabrics, muslin and the like, made with a first-rate, outlandishly styled thread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'etc' looks like part of the definition's list, but it is anagram fodder along with the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Coteline is a kind of fine corded muslin or cotton fabric, so the name of a cloth answers the cloth given.

clue.text: Thatcher’s bundle in yard, one surrounded by wood

indicators.note: something surrounded by another thing sits within it

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for yard
elm is a timber tree
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A roof-thatcher's bale lies in the yard, hemmed in by woodland.
explanation.walkthrough: Y followed by EL(A)M. 'Thatcher' is a roof-thatcher, not the former Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A yealm is a bundle of straw prepared and laid straight, ready for laying on a roof by a thatcher.

clue.text: Simpleton on ops getting muddled

indicators.note: muddled things are jumbled up, so these letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dimwit on military operations gets confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoon is an old slang and dialect word for a silly or foolish person, a ninny or dupe.

clue.text: Close point in lunar orbit – Roy adrift with epic ninth

indicators.note: something adrift has come loose and wanders, so these letters drift out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An astronaut called Roy drifts loose on an epic ninth mission near the Moon.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is built from Cynthia, a poetic name for the Moon, like perilune.
explanation.definitionFit: The pericynthion is the point of a lunar orbit nearest the Moon, the lunar equivalent of perigee.

clue.text: Some condone offences that will not be repeated

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run lying within them

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone forgives misdeeds on the understanding they will not happen again.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-off event happens only once, a single occurrence never repeated.

clue.text: Remove water bird in young oak

blocks.note: to flit is to move house, to remove in the old sense
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Someone shifts a waterbird into a sapling oak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as a container signal, but here it only joins definition and wordplay. To flit is British and Scots usage for moving house.
explanation.definitionFit: Flittern is a dialect word for a young oak tree, a sapling.

clue.text: Some knaves making millions in action

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: pas, a step in dancing, is taken as an action
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: Some rogues make millions through their activities.
explanation.walkthrough: PA(M)S. In the card game loo, pam is the jack of clubs, the highest trump; a jack is also called a knave.
explanation.definitionFit: Pam is the name for the jack of clubs in loo, so pams are particular knaves among playing cards.

clue.text: Almanac for e.g. solicitors working at wills

indicators.note: letters set working are put through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A legal yearbook for solicitors busy drawing up wills.
explanation.definitionFit: A law list is an annual directory of lawyers and legal information, a reference book for the profession.

clue.text: Chickens last but not as in blended soup

indicators.note: 'but not' tells you to take the named letters out of the word before
blending mixes things together, so these letters come out mixed up
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the letters to be mixed
taken as written, before two letters are removed

explanation.surface: Chicken lasts in a soup, though not as long as the other ingredients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not as' removes those two letters from the word before it, not from the soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Poults are young domestic fowl, chickens or turkeys, so the word names chicks in general.

clue.text: Kitchen dish: female bird in many gallons of old ale

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask, traditionally of 252 gallons of ale or wine
a ree or reeve is the female of the ruff

explanation.surface: A cook's dish in which a hen bird sits in a huge vat of ale.
explanation.walkthrough: TU(REE)N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tureen is a deep lidded bowl for serving soup, a piece of kitchen and table ware.

clue.text: Doctor-priest has converted follower

indicators.note: something converted has been changed in form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be changed
a man is a servant or follower of a master

explanation.surface: A clergyman with a medical background has won over a new disciple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' suits a priest winning souls, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer who also mediates with the spirit world, combining the roles of physician and holy man.

clue.text: Scripture held by Hindus as traditional

indicators.note: the letters are gripped inside the words that follow

blocks.note: a run of letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: Hindus regard a sacred text as part of tradition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sastra or shastra is a Hindu sacred treatise or body of religious law, a holy writing.

clue.text: Aquatic umbellifer is reduced by half in height

indicators.note: cutting a two-letter word by half leaves only one of its letters
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: sum is an old word for the summit or height of something
the first half of the word is

explanation.surface: A water plant's numbers are halved at altitude.
explanation.walkthrough: Sum for the top or height of something is an obsolete sense, as in summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sium is the genus of water parsnips, plants of the carrot family that grow in wet places.

clue.text: Pre-euro currency unit: notice king’s head on one

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: to mark is to notice
the opening letter of king
a means one

explanation.surface: An old coin bears a notice beside the king's portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'king's head' looks like the portrait on a coin, but it is just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The markka was the currency of Finland until the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Heads for Bhiwani in Haryana and Ranchi … herein?

definitions.text: Heads for Bhiwani in Haryana and Ranchi … herein?

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: the opening letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Travel directions to Indian towns, ending with a guess at the state they are in.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Bihar is an Indian state, and Ranchi was in it until Jharkhand split away in 2000, though Bhiwani is in Haryana, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Bihar is a state in eastern India, a region where such Indian towns might be found.

clue.text: Silver service always followed by another metal appendage

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
in tennis a let is a serve that must be replayed

explanation.surface: A silver tea service is always followed by another metal accessory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a set of silverware, but it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: An aglet is the metal tag on the end of a lace, a small metal piece attached to it.

clue.text: Recipe: crustacean (not cod) for beaks

indicators.note: the letters that follow are to be left out of the word before

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, from the Latin 'take'
an ostracod is a tiny bivalved crustacean
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: A recipe calls for shellfish but no cod, in place of the birds' bills.
explanation.walkthrough: OSTRACOD without COD leaves OSTRA. Beaks here are birds' bills, not judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostra is the plural of rostrum, a beak or beak-like snout, especially the prow of an ancient warship.

clue.text: Old-fashioned tonic, slushy stuff with a dash of alcohol

indicators.note: a dash is a small amount, here only the opening letter
with here means containing, holding the small piece within it

blocks.note: slop is sloppy, semi-liquid matter
the opening letter of alcohol

explanation.surface: A quaint pick-me-up turns out to be slush laced with a drop of booze.
explanation.walkthrough: S(A)LOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Salop, or saloop, was a hot drink made from sassafras or salep, drunk in the 18th and 19th centuries as a restorative.

clue.text: Thins something that may corrode a microlight?

blocks.note: to single seedlings is to thin them out, leaving one plant at each spot
a corrosive eats away at material

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what thins out or eats away a small light aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a microlight as an example, not a definition proper.
explanation.definitionFit: A microlight is a tiny light aircraft that often carries just its pilot, an example of a craft with room for one.

clue.text: Round buildings occupying central position among Romans?

indicators.note: only the letters that sit in the centre of the word are kept

blocks.note: Romans here are Roman Catholics, and the middle five letters of catholics are kept

explanation.surface: Domed buildings stand at the heart of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Romans must first become CATHOLICS, a step the question mark admits; its middle five letters are the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tholi is the plural of tholus, a circular domed building or beehive tomb in classical architecture.

clue.text: Try circling lake, calm

indicators.note: a word circling another goes all the way round it

blocks.note: to seek is to try or attempt
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to walk around a lake, staying serene.
explanation.walkthrough: SE(L)EK: the L goes inside SEEK.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleek can mean smooth and unruffled in manner, so it describes someone composed and untroubled.

clue.text: Source of vegetable oil? Find echoes in marsh plant

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
to ape is to mimic, and to echo someone is to copy them

explanation.surface: A botanist hunting the origin of a cooking oil hears echoes among the marsh plants.
explanation.walkthrough: R(APES)EED.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapeseed is crushed to make rapeseed or canola oil, one of the main cooking oils from plants.

clue.text: Judge, old or lacking in a witty riposte

indicators.note: the letters named are missing from the phrase that follows

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are removed
a retort is a sharp or witty reply

explanation.surface: A judge, long in the tooth, can't come up with a clever comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: A RETORT with OR removed leaves A RETT, one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arett is an obsolete Spenserian verb meaning to adjudge or assign, so it is an archaic word for judging.

clue.text: Year in pen – sad, broken and wheezing

indicators.note: one piece placed in another sits inside it
something broken is smashed apart, so these letters are put back in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A year in prison leaves an inmate miserable, shattered and short of breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyspnea is laboured or difficult breathing, the medical term for being breathless or wheezy.
